slides.0.title: The areas: what the register says
slides.0.subtitle: The place names are the boundaries
slides.1.title: The Cap Bon peninsula
slides.1.highlights.0.title: Kélibia
slides.1.highlights.0.content: A delimited area within Kélibia and Tazerka, in Nabeul governorate, registered for Muscat wine and Muscat mistelle
slides.1.highlights.1.title: Sidi Salem
slides.1.highlights.1.content: Khanguet and Beni Ayach, in the Grombalia delegation of Nabeul governorate, registered for red and rosé
slides.1.highlights.2.title: Where they are
slides.1.highlights.2.content: Kélibia is on the east side near the cape; Grombalia sits at the base of the peninsula, not far from the capital
slides.1.content: The two Cap Bon regions split into Muscat on one side and red and rosé on the other.
slides.2.title: South of the capital: Mornag
slides.2.highlights.0.title: Mornag's registered area
slides.2.highlights.0.content: Registered in 1974 as a VDQS: Mornag, Hammam-Lif and Kabouti, in what were then the governorates of Tunis and South Tunis, for red, rosé and white
slides.2.highlights.1.title: After 1989
slides.2.highlights.1.content: The area of AOC Mornag is set in the 1989 order, which this course could not read. Secondary sources say it is larger than the VDQS, but they differ, so it is not tested
slides.2.highlights.2.title: Grand Cru Mornag
slides.2.highlights.2.content: Its area is set in the 1977 order, which likewise could not be read, and it has no international registration
slides.2.content: The 1974 registration gives the clearest picture of Mornag; later changes depend on orders not read here.
slides.3.title: The north and inland
slides.3.highlights.0.title: Coteaux de Tébourba
slides.3.highlights.0.content: Tébourba, Schuiggui and Lansarine (then in South Tunis governorate) and Aïn-Targuellache (Bizerte), registered for red and rosé
slides.3.highlights.1.title: Thibar
slides.3.highlights.1.content: Muscat de Thibar covers Saint Joseph de Thibar in Béja governorate. Secondary sources say its vineyards were founded by the White Fathers (Pères Blancs)
slides.3.highlights.2.title: Coteaux d'Utique
slides.3.highlights.2.content: Named after the ancient city of Utique north of the capital. It has no international registration, so this course cannot confirm its area
slides.3.content: The governorates are those at registration in 1974; the map has changed since.
slides.4.componentProps.slide.title: 🧠 Knowledge check
Which region do Khanguet and Beni Ayach belong to?
In the Grombalia delegation of Nabeul.
The area lies within Kélibia and Tazerka.
Which region do Schuiggui and Lansarine belong to?
Along with Tébourba and Aïn-Targuellache in Bizerte.
What products was Mornag registered for in 1974?
Coteaux de Tébourba and Sidi Salem have only red and rosé.
